items.response:
I don't have the reasons in front of me, so I won't guess at why Nate won over the other two.
Action: Search your reno notes, the three quotes and related emails for the comparison, then send you a short summary Sam can read.

A Drumheller trip for the dinosaurs sounds great. I'll look for hotels for three nights and the Tyrrell child ticket price for Leo.
Action: Find hotels in Drumheller for three nights during March break week of the 16th and check Tyrrell's child admission, then send options. Tell me which nights and whether you're flying into Calgary and renting a car.

Good call to check. The last tally I have, from Nov 17, had you at $45,897 projected against the $48,000 budget, so $2,103 of headroom (4.4%), which is already well under a full 10% cushion. Your hunch may be right, but I haven't seen the revised quote yet.
Action: After the review, open Nate's revised quote, put it next to the Nov 17 numbers and the $48,000 budget, and show how much contingency is left.

I don't have the start time in front of me, so I'll check before telling you.
Action: Look up tonight's Leafs game start time and channel, and tell you if it starts before Leo's bedtime.

I don't have a note of what you said helps you unwind on weekends, so I won't make one up. A low-effort day is fine: something slow in the morning, a walk outside with Biscuit, and nothing booked.
Action: Search our past chats and notes for what you said helps, then build tomorrow's plan around it.

Holding the order. I don't have your basement kitchen setup in front of me, so I'll pull it rather than guess.
Action: Find your basement kitchen notes, list what you have to cook with, and suggest a few easy meals for the week.

This morning: added the dog walker Felipe to the pet budget, which puts monthly pet spend at about $729 against $350. I built the 'Payouts v2 launch risks (2025-11-12)' Notion page with six risks. October groceries and the August and September comparison are still being pulled.
Action: Send the grocery numbers when they come back.

Here's a draft: 'Team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. That is real money reaching real merchants, and it happened because of the care you all put in. Thank you.'
Action: Save it as a draft for you to post tomorrow. I won't post anything.

March really is a liar. Snow again, but at least it's a focus-block morning with no commute. My notes also have your passport expiring in March, so I'll check whether the renewal went through.
Action: Check the status of your passport renewal and tell you if it's still open.

Happy to, but I don't have the bakery or cake details from last time, so I won't guess.
Action: Search your email for the receipt or order confirmation for that cake, then reorder it for 31 Dec once I know the size and flavour, and confirm with you before paying.

Good question to ask before it renews. The answer comes from how much you actually spend there, not how it feels.
Action: Pull the past year of Costco charges from the card statements, total them by visit, compare against the membership fee on the renewal, and tell you whether it's worth keeping.

Spy series night works: Sunday 8:30 to 10 once Leo's down. For your mom's mithai, I'll look for well-reviewed Mumbai shops that deliver. It's kind of you to send something when she sounded low.
Action: Add a Sunday 20:30 to 22:00 block, then research Mumbai mithai shops with delivery and send a few options with box sizes. I'll need your mom's delivery address from your contacts to confirm.

Got it: text only, never call, and he starts at 7:30 am. I'll text: 'Hi Nate, quick check, are the cabinets still arriving Monday? Thanks, Riya.'
Action: Send that text to Nate, then pull all his invoices from your email into the reno sheet and tell you the total.

You should be proud. Leading Instant Payouts end to end as a senior PM and watching it work is a big deal, and saying it out loud counts.
Action: Save a line in your wins note so it's ready for your next review: shipped the Instant Payouts launch at Lumen Pay, May 2026, first project led end to end as a senior PM. Tell me if you'd rather I skip it.

All I know right now is that today Leo built a cushion fort that Biscuit took over, which may be fun but isn't a parcel idea. I don't have a saved list of what he's into, and I don't want to guess at food to skip, since allergies matter.
Action: Search your notes and past chats for Leo's current interests and any food restrictions, then draft a reply to Grace for you to approve.

Sure, a quick warm-up works. I don't have your recurring mistakes in front of me, so I'll check your lesson notes instead of quizzing you on the wrong things.
Action: Look through your Spanish notes and past quizzes for repeated errors and send a 9-question quiz before class. If I find nothing, I'll use a mix of ser/estar, por/para and gender.

I don't want to guess your exact job title for a benefits form, so I'll look it up in your records.
Action: Check your offer letter, HR profile or email signature for the official title, then draft a short areas-of-responsibility line from your recent work for you to approve.

Booking East End Plumbing for Monday morning, 29 Jun. For the Lattice self-review due Fri 10 Jul, I'll remind you to start on Tue 30 Jun and again on Mon 6 Jul.
Action: Book East End for Monday and confirm the arrival window, then set both Lattice reminders. Tell me if you'd prefer other days.

I don't have the drive time to Sam's parents' place in front of me, and Friday afternoon traffic can swing it a lot. Leaving right after pickup, I'll give you a range and refine it on the day.
Action: Look up the drive from home to Sam's parents' address for a departure right after pickup next Friday and send an estimated arrival range.

I don't have Tom's whisky saved anywhere I can see, and I won't guess a bottle. Posting the Slack message now.
Action: Post the draft in #payouts-launch, then search your notes and email for Tom's favourite whisky and send you what I find, or ask you if I come up empty.

Good timing to price it. For the August long weekend I'll check Fri 31 Jul to Tue 4 Aug, Toronto to Vancouver, for one traveller and for two.
Action: Pull rough return fares for direct flights, one traveller and two, and note when fares tend to jump. I won't book or set a price watch.

Good thought to check early. My notes have Leo's passport expiring in January and yours in March, each with a renewal planned, but I don't have confirmation that either was done. I also need Sam's.
Action: Check the expiry dates of all three passports against the Lisbon trip (18 to 30 Dec 2026), flag any that fall short of the validity needed, and tell you what's urgent.

I don't have a saved note of how you learn Spanish best or the vocab you want, so I won't make one up.
Action: Search your notes and past practice chats for your learning preferences and vocab themes, then set up tonight's session. If I find nothing, I'll ask you two quick questions.

I'll read Sam's text first, since I can't see it yet. No hotplate tonight, understood.
Action: Open Sam's text, then suggest two or three easy dinner options (a takeaway order or something that needs no hotplate) and let you pick.

On it. I'll write a short note Tanvi can use: guideline cap of 2.1% for 2026, anything above needs LTB approval, 90 days' written notice on Form N1, and she can pay the guideline amount if no application is made.
Action: Create the note with that summary and links to the official Ontario and LTB pages, and share it with you to forward.

Vale, quiz rápido de género. Escribe el o la: 1) ___ día 2) ___ foto 3) ___ tema 4) ___ moto 5) ___ idioma 6) ___ mapa 7) ___ mano 8) ___ sistema.
Action: Check your answers when you reply and explain any you miss.

Sending the text to Hannah. For Olivia's blurb, I'll keep it to 4-5 lines on what's in v1 and I won't put any dates in it without confirmation.
Action: Send the Hannah text, pull the v1 scope from the PRD and launch notes, and draft the blurb for you to review before it goes to Olivia.

Sleepover with Jun, pizza and a movie sounds great. I'll tell Hannah yes and put it on the family calendar for pickup at 3:30 until she brings Leo back tomorrow morning.
Action: Text Hannah a yes, add the family calendar event, and remind you before 3:30 to pack Leo's overnight bag.

Hola. Here's doctor's visit vocab in your Anki format from now on:
| Spanish | English | Example |
| el dolor | pain | Tengo dolor de cabeza. |
| la fiebre | fever | Tengo fiebre desde ayer. |
| la tos | cough | Tengo tos por la noche. |
| la receta | prescription | Necesito una receta. |
| el análisis de sangre | blood test | Me hicieron un análisis de sangre. |
Action: Save the table format as your default for vocab lists, and send a longer list for Tuesday's role-play with Carlos.

Added: Leo's swim lesson, every Tuesday at 17:30, Pam McConnell Aquatic Centre, starting tomorrow.
Action: None.
